title: Annual ryegrass round-bale silage post-storage dry-matter recovery and quality reference observations
citation: Crook, T., Stewart, B., Sims, M., Weiss, C., Coffey, K., Coblentz, W., & Beck, P. (2020). The effects of moisture at baling and wrapping delay on storage characteristics of annual ryegrass round bale silage. Crop, Forage & Turfgrass Management, 6(1), e20015. https://doi.org/10.1002/cft2.20015
source_locations: Table 2: post-storage outcomes by initial moisture treatment
Table 4: post-storage outcomes by wrapping delay
geography: University of Arkansas Southwest Research & Extension Center, Perrytown, Arkansas, USA
license: Article page accessible; no explicit reuse license identified in the accessible metadata. Values are factual table measurements transcribed with attribution; redistribution terms should be checked before external republishing.
material_scope: Annual ryegrass (Lolium multiflorum) wrapped round-bale silage in one field experiment. DRY treatment was cured 72 hours and had 38 ± 9.5% moisture at baling according to Methods and table notes (the abstract instead says 30 ± 9.5%); WET treatment had 74.6 ± 0.8% moisture. Bales were stored 85 days.
experimental_conditions: DRY n=18 and WET n=20 bales across wrapping delays of 0, 1, 2, and 3 days; four blocks. Four layers of 25-micrometer film. Table 2 gives means by moisture treatment pooled across wrapping delays. Table 4 gives means by wrapping delay pooled across moisture treatments. Table standard errors are reproduced as printed. Article reports no moisture-by-delay interaction for DM recovery; do not interpret pooled means as cell-level outcomes.
data_scope: 26 long-form records: Table 2 post-storage bale weight, dry-matter concentration, dry-matter recovery, pH, ammonia-N fraction, crude protein, and nonfibrous carbohydrate for DRY/WET moisture groups; Table 4 dry-matter recovery, pH, and ammonia-N fraction for 0–3 day wrapping delays.
limitations: Reference-only; not a roadside-grass or GreenHub storage calibration dataset and not a runtime default.
Single southeastern U.S. annual-ryegrass wrapped-bale experiment; material, climate, storage structure and scale differ from GreenHub loose or bulk roadside-grass storage.
Methods and table notes report 38 ± 9.5% moisture for DRY bales, while the abstract reports 30 ± 9.5%; preserve the conflict and do not silently resolve it.
Table 2 means are pooled over wrapping delay, and Table 4 means are pooled over moisture treatment; they are not factorial cell data and must not be joined as if paired.
Reported DM recovery is an aggregate endpoint. Composition concentrations do not establish component-specific mass recovery or gaseous/leachate losses.
Ammonia-N is the fraction of total nitrogen in silage, not an ammonia emission. NFC is calculated by difference and is not a direct sugar measurement.
Reported means and standard errors are not raw replicate observations; no kinetic curve or causal delay response is fitted from these aggregates.
conversion_or_processing: Transcribed reported Table 2 and Table 4 means and standard errors as printed. No conversion, imputation, interpolation, reconstruction of factorial cells, or kinetic fitting performed.
uncertainty: Table standard errors are retained. The paper reports n=18 DRY and n=20 WET bales, treatment allocation by block, and an 85-day storage period; raw replicate-level data were not extracted.
